title: Hierarchical page-bank and eviction skyline
author: Anika Sharma
description: Motivation: fragmentation and reactive spillovers continue to drive tail latency and unexpected OOMs on long-lived tenants with mixed-size keys. This PR introduces a hierarchical page-bank (HPB) allocator plus a lightweight eviction skyline planner to proactively reshape KV residency and smooth spill events. Summary: implement a page-granular bank that groups contiguous slab pages into hot/mid/cold lanes with fast in-place micro-compaction for small fragments; add a skyline-based eviction scorer that considers occupancy, write amplification risk, KV lifetime estimate, and downstream spill cost to prioritize candidates; integrate with the serving scheduler to allow preemptive async spill tasks and to mark lanes with temporary admission control. Design details: (1) HPB allocator: pages are tagged with lane metadata and a compacted-run map; allocation prefers hot lane for small sizes, cold lane for large allocations, and migrates low-touch fragments via bounded micro-compaction passes to coalesce free runs without full GC. The allocator exposes new metrics (lane_fill_pct, run_count, microcompact_ops/s). (2) Eviction skyline: a multi-dimensional score computed at eviction-time combining recency, per-key residency delta, estimated recompute cost (model KV warmup), and hypothetical downstream I/O latency; the skyline planner produces a ranked candidate list and supports batch evictions with spill hysteresis to avoid repeated small writes. (3) Scheduler integration: a low-priority async compaction worker pool that performs micro-compaction and coordinated spill with backoff; admission control can hold low-priority batches when lane_fill_pct exceeds configured thresholds. Backwards compatibility: all new behavior gated behind feature flag "hpbank_eviction_skyline" and defaulted off for existing Dedicated customers. Checklist: implement allocator core + API, skyline scorer, scheduler hooks, metrics, end-to-end integration tests, benchmark harness runs, docs and migration notes, feature-flag gating, and rollback switch. Testing: unit + fuzz for allocator invariants, stress tests with mixed-size synthetic workloads (zipf + large object injection), deterministic replay of an in-production incident trace that previously caused spill storms; stability verified across 72h soak on staging cluster. Benchmarks: p95 latency for small (<=64B) token fetches reduced by 18% under 20k qps steady workload with 40% large-object churn; sustained memory reclamation improved: average resident fragmentation dropped from 24% to 9% in high-churn tests; aggregate write bandwidth to spill storage fell 35% under the incident trace. Rollback plan: flip feature flag off, drain compaction workers, and run a light allocator compaction to restore pre-change placement; alert runbook updated to include expected metrics to observe (lane_fill_pct, skyline_rejects, spill_backlog). Related work: follows on ideas from ENG-1320 (adaptive slab) and borrows scoring heuristics from previous spillback dampener experiments. Files changed: allocator core, eviction planner, scheduler hooks, metrics, tests, and docs. Merge strategy: squash merge after green CI and 2 approvals.
commits: Introduce HPB allocator core (allocator/hpb_core.rs): lane metadata and run map
Add skyline eviction planner (kv/eviction/skyline.cpp): multi-dimensional scorer and batch emitter
Scheduler hooks and worker pool (scheduler/compaction_worker.go): async micro-compaction
Feature flag, toggles, and metrics export (telemetry/metrics.go): lane_fill_pct, skyline_scores
Add unit and integration tests (tests/kv_hpb_integration.py and tests/skyline_fuzz.go)
Fix race in allocator free list and add defensive assertions
review_comments: Marcus Lee: Can you clarify the compaction work budget and how it interacts with CPU quotas on Dedicated nodes? The code looks safe but we need a throttle to avoid noisy neighbor effects.
Anika Sharma: Added a per-node compaction_budget_ms config, default 50ms per sweep, and tied it to the scheduler token bucket; documented in deploy notes.
Tessa Nguyen: The skyline score includes recompute cost—how do you estimate it for cold keys? Consider a cheaper default to avoid over-eviction.

Anika Sharma: Skyline uses a decayed histogram from access traces; for unknown keys we fall back to a conservative recompute estimate (10ms) and weight it low; added tests showing behavior on cold-key eviction.
Diego Alvarez: CI showed intermittent integration flakiness on macOS builders for the fuzz harness.
Anika Sharma: Adjusted harness to be deterministic on macOS by seeding RNG and widened timeouts; re-run CI and passed.
release_notes: Add hierarchical page-bank allocator and skyline eviction planner to reduce fragmentation and spill events. Feature gated behind hpbank_eviction_skyline. Expected benefits: lower p95 latency for small fetches, reduced spill bandwidth, and lower fragmentation for mixed-size workloads.
benchmarks_summary: Steady-state micro-benchmark: small-key p95 -18% at 20k qps; fragmentation median dropped from 24% to 9%; spill write throughput -35% on incident trace; compaction CPU overhead measured at ~2.1% of node CPU under default budget.
